extraction.name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI)
extraction.description: A multimodal benchmark comprising 20,000 conflicting instructions evenly distributed between language-language and vision-language paradigms, designed to evaluate the capability of large multimodal models to recognize self-contradictory instructions across 8 tasks.
extraction.creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, and Dequan Wang
extraction.publisher: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Fudan University, Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed using an automatic dataset creation framework called AutoCreate that leverages programs and large language models. The process starts with manually input seeds and automatically generates data through two loops (Language Loop and Visual Loop), each processed by a Generator, Decorator, and Cleaner. Human experts rigorously checked the quality of the generated dataset. For vision-language conflicts, image captions were modified to introduce conflicts. The SemanticConflict task was based on the ImageNet dataset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of manually created seeds for each task type, and for the SemanticConflict task, images and labels from the ImageNet dataset. The seeds include short sentences, rules, attribute descriptions, instruction pairs, geometric shapes, and entity-related numerical data depending on the specific conflict type.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human experts rigorously checked the quality of the AutoCreate-generated dataset. The data undergoes quality checks by human experts after generation, with manual selection of subsets (SCI-Base at 10% and SCI-Core at 1% of SCI-All).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Both human experts and LLMs are involved in double-checking the quality of the generated dataset. The Cleaner component removes data that does not meet quality standards.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Large Language Models (LLMs) are used in the AutoCreate framework for automatic dataset generation. The framework includes a Generator, Decorator, and Cleaner that leverage LLMs to create and process data. For vision-language conflicts, image captions are modified to introduce conflicts.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark only includes language-language and vision-language paradigms, lacks fine-grained control to determine conflict degree, and does not provide detailed study on attention mechanisms of large multimodal models when confronted with conflict instructions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work provides researchers with a standardized platform to assess and enhance LMMs' ability to navigate conflicting instructions, advancing human-computer interaction. The AutoCreate framework facilitates creation of diverse instruction datasets, promoting inclusivity in AI research. By improving dissonance detection, the approach boosts LMM performance and fosters trust and reliability in AI systems, essential for societal integration.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is designed to evaluate the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) to detect conflicting instructions and comprehend self-contradictory instructions effectively.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: More modalities will be included in the SCI benchmark based on the automatic framework AutoCreate in future updates.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data manipulation includes substitution and alteration techniques across different conflict types. For FigureConflict, numerical data is manipulated by changing maximum values to minimum values. For GeometricConflict, descriptive phrases are modified to refer to non-existent objects. For SemanticConflict, correct labels are substituted with similar but different objects. Images vary in font, size, and color to augment diversity.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset creation follows a generator-decorator-cleaner pipeline. The Generator creates initial language/vision data, the Decorator creates self-contradictions in the generated data, and the Cleaner removes data that does not meet quality standards. Both human experts and LLMs are involved in double-checking the quality of the generated dataset. Human experts rigorously checked the quality of the AutoCreate-generated dataset.
